tools.name: get_entry
tools.description: One entry, by VHID, short name or Wikidata QID: its public record (title, description, handles, image, URL) and, as `editing`, what the editor would load for this key — the current revision, the editable fields, every handle with who manages it (the Wikidata sync or the site), which fields the sync

tools.name: search_entries
tools.description: Search the entries as the site search does: words match titles, subtitles and descriptions; a Wikidata QID finds the entries linked to it; a VHID finds that entry and the entries that link to it.

tools.name: find_by_handle
tools.description: Which public entries list a handle: “is x.com/someone an official account, and whose?”. Give a profile’s address as url (https://x.com/someone), or platform (its catalog id: twitter, instagram, youtube, …) and value (someone or @someone). Answers each entry’s VHID, title and URL, the handle as the e

tools.name: get_entry_history
tools.description: An entry’s public edit history, newest first (`next_offset` pages on). A merged entry’s key gives its own history.

tools.name: get_entries
tools.description: Up to 50 entries’ public records in one call, by VHID or short name (not a Wikidata QID: get_entry or search_entries finds an entry by its item), each answered as get_entry answers it signed out — the entry, or not_found — in the order given. A name given twice is answered once.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_entry, find_by_handle · Private data: get_entry, get_entries · Public sink: find_by_handle.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_entry, find_by_handle · Private data: get_entry, get_entries · Public sink: find_by_handle

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
